daughter felt unwell yesterday and we thought it was a UTI. The pharmacist was worried about the amount of pain in her kidney area and said she needed to be seen by the GP. So, she called the GP and told them, wouldn’t see her no appointments. She was crying with pain so called 111 who said call your GP back, tell them we have assessed you and you need to be seen by primary care within two hours. So we call, refused to see her telling us ‘out of hours are legally obliged to see you’
The clue is in the name, OUT OF HOURS! It is not out of hours, you are open, and whilst I fully understand you do not have endless appointments, as a prior manager in a GP surgery I am also aware if 111 say you need to be seen the GP has to see you. I am also aware the rude receptionist could have sent a task to the GP to get advice but that wasn’t even offered, I am also aware certain things SHOULD NOT BE REFUSED by the GP, mental health, palliative, children and suspected infections. You have broken many rules here.We have spoken to 111 again, who have told us we will have to call them back at 6.30 so they can access the out of hours appointments and book her in, because you should see her!!!!
If this was a normal UTI we could drop a sample in, but as you know when it is a suspected kidney infection you have to be seen.
I suggest you advise your receptionist that OOH is what it says .
